LESSON: READING ALOUD (ARTICULATION)

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.1: Reading Aloud (Articulation)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Aloud (Articulation), part of Reading in Grade 5 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify German sound combinations in reading,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud (Articulation) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read dialogues for communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud (Articulation) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the importance of turn taking in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud (Articulation) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify German sound combinations in reading,

   Reading Aloud (Articulation) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read dialogues for communication,

   Reading Aloud (Articulation) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the importance of turn taking in communication.

   Reading Aloud (Articulation) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read along to recorded dialogues on basic greetings and saying of own name from a variety of sources,

2. read short dialogues on basic greetings and saying own name aloud,

3. read simple dialogues on basic greetings and saying own name aloud with peers,

4. read aloud texts in turns and record themselves to listen to their own intonation and articulation.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read along to recorded dialogues on basic greetings and saying of own name from a variety of sources,
2. read short dialogues on basic greetings and saying own name aloud,
3. read simple dialogues on basic greetings and saying own name aloud with peers,
4. read aloud texts in turns and record themselves to listen to their own intonation and articulation.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading Aloud (Articulation) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: The learner develops fluency as they clearly read dialogues on saying own name in pairs

Values:
Unity: The learner works collaboratively as they read aloud dialogue with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Self-esteem: The learner develops confidence as they read aloud texts in turns and record themselves to listen to their own

intonation and articulation.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner links the concept of greetings and introductions to the same concept in English and Kiswahili.
